ca_upper_main_wall.blurb: Upper Main Wall is the higher tier of the central face at Invisible Wall, in the hills above Santa Barbara. A ledge walkway cuts across the face and separates it into a lower and an upper half, and many of the lines can be strung together into two-pitch outings. There are eight routes, five sport and three trad. Most sit between 5.7 and 5.10, with a cluster of 5.9s, plus a couple of very easy trad lines around 5.2 and 5.4 that suit newer leaders. The wall is one of several sectors at Invisible Wall, so it combines easily with neighbouring faces for a longer day.

ca_treasure_chest_boulder.blurb: Treasure Chest Boulder is a single large block in Treasure Cove, a bouldering pocket on Castle Peak in the Donner and Truckee area near Lake Tahoe, set among Sierra forest. It holds eight problems with a wide spread of difficulty: one at the easiest end, a few in the V2 to V5 range (three of them V4), and a short run of hard ones reaching V7 and V8. The boulder is the large, obvious one on the left as you drop into the cove, so it works as a first stop before exploring the rest of the area.

ca_y_boulder.blurb: Y Boulder is the lower of the Saddle Boulders, a small bouldering group sitting on a saddle between two higher hills in the Nut Tree and Hillcrest boulder zone above Vacaville. It takes its name from the obvious Y-shaped crack that splits it. The boulder has eight problems from V0 up to V6, with three at V3 and a couple at V5, so a visit suits climbers across the moderate range as well as those after something harder. The uphill-facing parts of the saddle blocks are not steep and give easy walk-offs, while the steeper sides carry a few very overhanging problems.

ca_yabo_zone.blurb: Yabo Zone is a bouldering sector at Castle Rock State Park in the Santa Cruz Mountains, on the Castle Rock loop. It is a cluster of sandstone boulders, some tall and some low, with eight problems in total. Grades run from V0 to V8: a handful of easy to moderate lines, one around V4, and two hard ones at V7 and V8. The problems include a short overhanging bulge with a sit start, a sloper arete and a groove line, and a highball. Sandstone here breaks easily when damp, so dry conditions matter.

ca_angel_wings.blurb: Angel Wings is a huge backcountry wall at about 9,500 feet in Sequoia and Kings Canyon National Parks, above the Hamilton Lakes basin. It stands as the biggest rock face in the Sierra outside Yosemite, roughly 3,000 feet tall, and the hike in is around 16 miles from the nearest road, so trips here are multi-day. There are seven routes, all trad or alpine in style, running from 5.9 up to 5.11, and the longest take 12 to 17 pitches. It is a serious objective for experienced parties rather than a casual crag.
